what_is_wrong: Two counts in seepage_calibration.json describe the segment set of all 15 matched districts, not the 14 districts that were fitted. One matched district, HCWCID#18, has no authorised water in the 1998 table, so it has no loss and entered no fit and no test; its 4 segments (5.0 km) are counted all the same.
wrong_fields: segments_kept says 3534. The fit and the held-out test used 3530 segments.
km_kept says 3488.4. The fit and the held-out test used 3483.4 km.
also_stated_here: The declaration in reports/decision.md and ARCHITECTURE.md expected 18 districts. 14 were fitted: 4 districts in the 1998 table could not be matched to a district in the map by name without guessing (Adams Garden, HCMUD, HCWID#3 (McAllen), Santa Maria), and 1 matched district has no authorised water (HCWCID#18). The 1998 table has 19 rows.

The pass statistic is the DIFFERENCE OF MEDIANS: the rival's median held-out error minus the model's median held-out error, recomputed on each resample of districts. It is not the median of the per-district differences.
effect_on_results: None. Every fitted factor, held-out error, rank correlation, bootstrap interval and the pass or fail outcome was computed on the 14 fitted districts only and is unchanged.
why_a_separate_file: Frozen result files are not rewritten. seepage_calibration.json is left exactly as the run wrote it.
fixed_in_code: seepage_calibration.calibration_item now writes the fitted districts' own counts in segments_kept, km_kept and class_counts_in_the_set, and lists matched districts that have no loss separately.
